title: Extension doc-set navigation tree (docs-tree.json)

audience.$comment: The docs.md audience split, closed: 'user' pages live under docs/user/ (or the set's user section), 'dev' pages under docs/dev/sdk/ (or the set's authoring section). No third audience exists.

chapterSlug.$comment: The plan-34 chapter taxonomy, closed and family-wide (guidelines/extension-docs.md is the law). 'chapters' is the conformance marker: optional, but when a set declares it, it declares exactly the ten — never missing chapters.

docsCategory.$comment: The per-extension category vocabulary, CLOSED (the extensionDocsTree form's law — guidelines/extension-docs.md). Derived from health's four real builtin trees: 'Getting Started' → overview/setup, 'Sync' + 'Using the Bridge' → usage, 'Advanced' → reference, 'Security' → security, 'Help' → troubleshooting (added to the proposal because every real tree carries a troubleshooting page), plus changelog for per-extension release notes. A real page that fits none of these ADDS a slug here (family decision, canonical-first + re-sync) — it never reopens free-form categories. Closed ≠ mandatory: a tree lists only the categories it has pages for.

i18n.$comment: Nav-label i18n, SAME shape/conventions as the extension manifest's i18n block (locale pattern, 16 locales, 400 keys/values) — the family string rule: labels resolve through the host locale, never hardcoded per-render. Optional everywhere: a single-locale tree keeps its titles inline and stays valid. Key naming is the set's choice; completeness beyond 'defaultLocale + locales' is wall/validator-owned per product (deliberately not schema-checked).

id.$comment: Stable and unique across the whole tree (uniqueness is wall-checked — JSON Schema cannot express it).

file.$comment: Path RELATIVE to the tree's own directory; never absolute. Existence is wall-checked, not schema-checkable. The §10.9 page-locale convention (<page>.<locale>.md siblings, noted per item) applies to extension-doc pages; this chaptered form notes locales only when it adopts the docsItem.locales field.

then.$comment: A leaf node (no children) MUST reference its doc file; a grouping node may carry one as a section index.

project.$comment: The doc set's slug (product or SDK name), not necessarily the repo slug — e.g. 'career-connector-sdk'.

chapters.$comment: Chapter-conformance marker, optional but validated when present: exactly the ten taxonomy slugs (cross-tree node ids SHOULD mirror them — the wall checks declared chapters have matching node ids).

chapteredTree.$comment: The plan-34 form every SDK-grade doc set adopts (waves 2-6). The ten-chapter skeleton at templates/docs-set/ is the reference instance.

id.$comment: Stable and unique across the whole tree (uniqueness is wall-checked).

file.$comment: Path RELATIVE to the tree's own directory; never absolute. Existence is wall-checked, not schema-checkable. Page-locale convention (§10.9): this names the DEFAULT-locale page; translations are siblings named <page>.<locale>.md and are NOT listed here — the item's optional `locales` array notes them.

locales.$comment: Page-locale convention (§10.9, owner decision 2026-10-19 — the tree NOTES per-page available locales): each entry declares a <page>.<locale>.md sibling beside the default page. Append-only addition (per-extension docs form); the chaptered form adopts it when a set ships translated pages. A noted locale without its sibling file is a broken promise — wall/validator-owned (existence beside the tree), same discipline as `file`. A page noting NO locales is the honest single-locale case.

audience.$comment: Optional per-item audience tag (the chaptered form's closed enum): 'user' pages explain the extension to its user, 'dev' pages to the person hacking on it. Absent = untagged (renders everywhere); never a third audience.

index.$comment: Landing override (the landing rule): array order is render order and the FIRST item of the FIRST category is the landing page by default; 'index: true' on exactly ONE item across the whole tree overrides that. The exactly-one count is wall/validator-owned (JSON Schema cannot count siblings).

title.$comment: Display override for the category slug; absent = the host derives the label (title-cased slug) or resolves it through the i18n map. Each category slug appears AT MOST ONCE per tree (wall-checked — uniqueItems cannot express it over objects).

categories.$comment: Array order is render order; the first item of the first category is the landing page unless exactly one item carries index: true (the landing rule).

extensionDocsTree.$comment: THE per-extension documentation form (every bundle, builtin or imported): a docs/ dir at the bundle root, this tree at docs/docs-tree.json, markdown pages beside it, bound by the manifest's optional 'docs' pointer (extension-manifest.schema.json). Renamed from legacyCategoryList when the closed category vocabulary landed (2026-10-19, plan 34 wave 7): the free-form 'Getting Started'-style category strings it accepted are REJECTED now — real categories mapped into the closed set instead (health's four builtin trees migrated same-wave). The per-extension skeleton at templates/extension-docs/ is the reference instance.

$comment: STRUCTURAL GATE ONLY — the docs-tree contract of plan 34 / guidelines/extension-docs.md. Two forms, never mixed in one artifact: chapteredTree (SDK-grade doc sets) and extensionDocsTree (per-extension docs, closed categories). Beyond structure, wall/validator-owned (deliberately NOT schema-checked): node/item-id uniqueness across a tree; every 'file' resolves to an existing .md next to the tree; every item-noted 'locales' entry has its <page>.<locale>.md sibling beside the tree (§10.9 page-locale convention — resolution is best-locale then defaultLocale, hosts state what they served); declared 'chapters' have matching node ids; category slugs at most once per extensionDocsTree; 'index: true' on at most one item (exactly the landing rule's override); i18n key completeness when a product needs locale coverage; docs.md page rules (one H1, opening paragraph, relative links) which apply to every page a tree references — plus the markdown law: no raw HTML in extension-doc pages (hosts strip/sanitize like the sites do post-H3; code fences and spans are exempt). The PRODUCT-level docs/docs-tree.json of guidelines/docs.md (audiences -> categories -> items) is NOT this contract's scope — different file, different law, never mix the two shapes in one artifact.
